input.quote: and (d) any breach of any representations, warranties or covenants by Array in Article 15 above, except to the extent such Third Party Claims result from the gross negligence or willful misconduct of a Ono Indemnitee.
input.rationale: The Agreement has a mutual indemnity architecture (16.1 Ono indemnifies Array; 16.2 Array indemnifies Ono) with standard notice/control/cooperation and settlement-consent procedure in 16.3, so procedure is fine. However, Array's indemnity in 16.2 is limited to Array Territory product activities, Array-sponsored Clinical Studies and breaches of Array's Article 15 representations; it contains no limb for third-party claims that the Products or our exercise of the licensed Array Patents/Know-How infringe or misappropriate third-party IP. Article 15 gives no non-infringement warranty and 15.4 expressly disclaims one, and Section 11.4 leaves each party to defend patent Infringement Actions at its own expense, so no route exists to recover from the licensor. Meanwhile our own indemnity in 16.1(a) captures any and all Liabilities from Third Party Claims arising from our Ono Territory commercialization, which on its face includes third-party IP infringement claims against Array. That is the walk-away pattern under this rule (no licensor IP indemnity, with a one-way customer indemnity covering the licensed subject matter) and fails the fallback, which requires at minimum a vendor IP indemnity (usual exclusions/remedies, cap acceptable). The redline adds an IP infringement limb 16.2(e) and a matching carve-out from 16.1(a); the comment flags that usual exclusions (our modifications/combinations) or a cap on this limb are acceptable fallbacks.

proposal.summary: Add Array IP-infringement indemnity limb to Section 16.2 and carve IP claims out of Ono's Section 16.1(a) indemnity
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Array's indemnity in Section 16.2 covers only Array Territory activities, Array-sponsored studies and Article 15 breaches, so no party stands behind third-party IP infringement claims arising from our exercise of the licensed Array Patents and Know-How (and Section 15.4 disclaims any non-infringement warranty), while our Section 16.1(a) indemnity captures every Third Party Claim from our Ono Territory activities, including such IP claims. We have added an IP infringement limb to Array's indemnity and a matching carve-out from ours; we can discuss the usual exclusions (our modifications or combinations) or a cap on this limb as a fallback.
